---
title: App Builder SDK
description: TypeScript SDK for building workspace apps — five primitives, typed integration calls, automatic MCP surfacing.
---

`@holaboss/app-builder-sdk` is the package new Holaboss workspace apps build against. It centers on five orthogonal primitives that compose into any app shape — publishing, messaging, workflow, event-driven, sync-mirror — with no `as any` in app code and no ad-hoc retry or scheduling logic leaking out of the SDK.

The canonical source lives at `sdk/app-builder-sdk/src/`.

## Install

```bash
bun install @holaboss/app-builder-sdk
# or
npm install @holaboss/app-builder-sdk
```

The package targets Node.js 20+ and is authored in TypeScript.

## The five primitives

```ts
const app = createApp({ id: "slack", provider: SLACK })

app.connection()              // declare the app needs an integration binding
app.resource(name, def)       // a typed row with its own state machine
app.action(resource, name, …) // a state transition + upstream API call
app.sync(name, def)           // periodic upstream read → upsert local rows
app.start()                   // validate config; the runtime drives execution
```

| Primitive | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `connection()` | Tells the runtime which provider binding the app needs |
| `resource()` | Defines a typed row — Zod schema + state alphabet + emit rules |
| `action()` | A state transition; receives `{ bridge, row }`, calls upstream APIs |
| `sync()` | Periodic fetch + upsert; **scheduling lives in the Holaboss automations layer, not in the SDK** |
| `start()` | Boot; validates the registered config |

Full type contract: `sdk/app-builder-sdk/src/types.ts`. Public exports: `sdk/app-builder-sdk/src/index.ts`.

## Transports — auth is pluggable

The SDK never assumes a specific provider auth flow. `BridgeClient` delegates network I/O to a `TransportFn` and the package bundles three transport implementations:

| Transport | When to use | What you supply |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createBearerTokenTransport` | Self-host OAuth — you manage tokens (Auth0, Clerk, your own auth server) | `accessToken: string \| () => Promise<string>` |
| `createComposioDirectTransport` | Direct to Composio, no broker hop — local dev, E2E, single-tenant | `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` + `connectedAccountId` |
| `createRuntimeBrokerTransport` | **Production** — app running inside a Holaboss workspace runtime | `provider` slug; runtime injects `HOLABOSS_INTEGRATION_BROKER_URL` + `HOLABOSS_APP_GRANT` |

Roll your own with ~20 lines of `fetch` returning `{ status, body, headers }` for custom auth (Vault, mTLS, internal gateway).

## Runtime teammate tasks

Use `createTeammateClient()` when an app needs to trigger delegated agent work inside the current workspace and track it as a first-class task.

Choose the execution model per action:

- Use direct provider integration via `createRuntimeBrokerTransport({ provider })` when the app can perform the side effect deterministically from structured app state.
- Use `providerEffectAction(...)` to encode those deterministic provider side effects in the SDK action layer.
- Use teammate tasks when the work is open-ended, tool-heavy, multi-step, interruptible, or needs agent judgment.
- Use `delegatedTaskAction(...)` to encode delegated agent work in the SDK action layer.
- For mixed flows, use teammate tasks for drafting/research/classification and direct integration for the final provider side effect.

Decision procedure:

1. Classify the action as one of:
   - `deterministic_provider_effect`
   - `agentic_work`
   - `mixed_flow`
2. Check whether the exact provider path is available in principle:
   - the provider exists in the runtime integration catalog
   - the app can declare it in `app.runtime.yaml`
   - the app can build the exact payload from app state
   - the provider action matches the app's ownership model
3. Choose the architecture:
   - `deterministic_provider_effect` + provider path available in principle -> direct integration
   - `agentic_work` -> teammate task
   - `mixed_flow` -> teammate first, direct integration second

Important constraint:

- A provider not being connected during the build turn is not, by itself, a reason to switch the design to teammate execution.
- If the correct architecture is a direct provider action, still wire the app around `createRuntimeBrokerTransport({ provider })`, declare the integration in `app.runtime.yaml`, and surface the blocked state through integration readiness so the user can connect or reconnect the provider.

Examples:

- "Send this approved email" -> direct Gmail integration
- "Draft a personalized cold email" -> teammate task
- "Create this exact Linear issue" -> direct Linear integration
- "Research and summarize today's news" -> teammate task

Anti-pattern:

- Do not delegate a deterministic provider side effect just because there was an approval step. If the app already has the exact reviewed payload and a connected provider, prefer the integration path.
- Do not replace a direct integration design with teammate execution just because the provider is not connected during the build turn. Missing auth or binding should surface as a blocked product state that asks the user to connect the provider.
- Do not treat teammate execution as the generic low-risk fallback when integration setup is uncertain. The fallback should preserve the intended product ownership model.

```ts title="src/server/send-approved-email.ts"
import {
  providerEffectAction,
} from "@holaboss/app-builder-sdk"

app.action(draft, "send", providerEffectAction({
  provider: "gmail",
  fromStates: ["approved"],
  toState: "sent",
  blockedState: "send_blocked",
  failedState: "send_failed",
  buildRequest: ({ row }) => ({
    to: row.email,
    subject: row.subject,
    body: row.body,
  }),
  execute: async ({ bridge, request }) =>
    bridge.call("POST", "/messages/send", request),
  persistBlocked: (blocked) => ({
    blocker_code: blocked.code,
    blocker_message: blocked.message,
  }),
  persistSuccess: ({ result }) => ({
    provider_message_id: result.id,
  }),
}))
```

```ts title="src/server/news-report.ts"
import { createTeammateClient } from "@holaboss/app-builder-sdk"

const teammateClient = createTeammateClient()

const roster = await teammateClient.teammates.list()
const general = roster.teammates.find((entry) => entry.teammate_id === "general")

const task = await teammateClient.tasks.create({
  title: "Generate latest news report",
  description: "Research today's major news and save a concise report back into the app.",
  status: "todo",
  assigneeTeammateId: general?.teammate_id ?? null,
  execution: {
    turnContext: {
      sessionId: "session-main",
      inputId: "input-main",
    },
  },
})

const refreshed = await teammateClient.tasks.get(task.task_id)
```

Current behavior:

- `tasks.create()` uses the durable issue route first, then hydrates the richer runtime task payload.
- `tasks.list()` and `tasks.get()` include `active_run` and `latest_run` so the app can inspect execution state directly.
- `reply()`, `rerun()`, and `cancel()` map onto the same task lifecycle controls the runtime uses internally.
- `execution.turnContext` is optional, but when the app can provide `sessionId` and `inputId` the delegated run stays attached to the originating turn instead of becoming an orphaned background run.
- Model selection is runtime-owned; the teammate SDK does not expose app-level model override fields.
- `parentTaskId` models task hierarchy, while `blockedBy` models execution dependencies and workflow ordering.

### Workflow dependencies

For multi-step teammate workflows, use `blockedBy` on the downstream task. Do not rely on `parentTaskId` alone when execution order matters.

```ts title="src/server/workflow.ts"
await teammateClient.tasks.create({
  title: "Build dashboard UI",
  status: "todo",
  assigneeTeammateId: "frontend",
  parentTaskId: "ISS-10", // optional tree structure only
  blockedBy: [
    {
      task_id: "ISS-9",
      relation: "handoff",
      instruction: "Continue from the API contract task.",
    },
  ],
})
```

Practical guidance:

- Persist each created task id onto app-owned rows so later actions can attach deterministic workflow edges.
- Use `relation: "handoff"` when the downstream task should continue from the upstream output.
- Use `relation: "input"` when the downstream task should treat the upstream output as source input.

### Standard pattern for button-driven teammate work

For app-owned agent flows, prefer the SDK's higher-level delegation helpers over custom task glue:

- `delegatedTaskAction(...)` turns teammate dispatch into a normal app action and persists task identifiers back onto the row.
- `createLocalAppActionApi(...)` exposes those actions over a standard local HTTP endpoint for the app UI.

```ts title="src/server/report-actions.ts"
import {
  createLocalAppActionApi,
  delegatedTaskAction,
} from "@holaboss/app-builder-sdk"

app.action(reportRequest, "delegate_latest_news", delegatedTaskAction({
  fromStates: ["ready"],
  toState: "delegated",
  buildTask: ({ row }) => ({
    title: row.title,
    description: "Research today's major news and save a concise report back into the app.",
    status: "todo",
    assigneeTeammateId: "general",
  }),
  persistTask: {
    taskId: "delegated_task_id",
    issueId: "delegated_issue_id",
    sessionId: "delegated_session_id",
  },
}))

const localActions = createLocalAppActionApi({ app, bridge })
```

For workflow steps, `buildTask(...)` can return `blockedBy` using previously persisted task ids:

```ts title="src/server/workflow-actions.ts"
app.action(reportRequest, "delegate_dashboard_ui", delegatedTaskAction({
  fromStates: ["ready"],
  toState: "delegated",
  buildTask: ({ row }) => ({
    title: row.title,
    status: "todo",
    assigneeTeammateId: "frontend",
    blockedBy: row.api_contract_task_id
      ? [
          {
            task_id: row.api_contract_task_id,
            relation: "handoff",
            instruction: "Continue from the API contract task.",
          },
        ]
      : [],
  }),
  persistTask: {
    taskId: "dashboard_task_id",
  },
}))
```

Expose these standard local endpoints from the app's HTTP server:

- `GET /__holaboss/actions/health`
- `POST /__holaboss/actions/run`

If the app uses teammate-triggering UI, also declare a `smoke_tests:` entry in `app.runtime.yaml`. `workspace_apps_ensure_running` executes these probes after startup and fails if the delegated task path is broken or returns invalid runtime metadata.

```yaml title="app.runtime.yaml"
smoke_tests:
  - name: queue_latest_news_task
    kind: delegated_task_action
    payload:
      action_name: delegate_latest_news
      resource_name: report_request
      row_status: ready
      row_data:
        title: "Smoke latest news"
    expect:
      row_status: delegated
      task_statuses:
        - todo
      run_statuses:
        - queued
```

## A minimal app

```ts title="src/app.ts"
import { createApp, z } from "@holaboss/app-builder-sdk"
import { SLACK } from "./provider.ts"

const app = createApp({ id: "slack", provider: SLACK })

app.connection()

const message = app.resource("message", {
  schema: z.object({
    channel_id: z.string(),
    text: z.string(),
  }),
  states: ["draft", "sent"] as const,
  initialState: "draft",
  emit: { surface: "outputs" },
})

app.action(message, "send", {
  fromStates: ["draft"],
  toState: "sent",
  run: async ({ row, bridge }) => {
    const r = await bridge.call<{ ts: string }>("POST", "/chat.postMessage", {
      channel: row.channel_id,
      text: row.text,
    })
    if (r.kind === "error") throw r
    return { external_id: r.data.ts }
  },
})

app.start()
```

## What the SDK normalizes for you

- Upstream HTTP status → typed `BridgeError` codes (`rate_limited`, `not_connected`, `not_found`, `validation_failed`, `upstream_error`) so app code pattern-matches instead of string-parsing responses.
- Per-provider `baseUrl` + `allowedHosts` enforced **before** the transport runs — endpoint typos fail fast, never reach the network.
- MCP tool list auto-derived from declared actions; no hand-rolled `tools/list` handler.
- Resource state changes emit workspace outputs / session artifacts automatically based on the resource's `emit` configuration.

## What's deliberately out of scope

- **Scheduling and retry.** Those live in the Holaboss automations layer. `sync.schedule` strings are descriptive, not executed by the SDK.
- **A scaffolder.** New apps copy a reference app, or get built end-to-end via the `app_builder` agent skill — see [Build Your First App](/docs/build/apps/first-app).
- **Per-app SKILL.md.** Holaboss's skill system is system-wide (`runtime/harnesses/.../embedded-skills/`) or workspace-local (`<workspace>/skills/`). App-local markdown is not a skill.

## Reference apps

Five reference apps under `sdk/app-builder-sdk/reference/` demonstrate the SDK across shapes:

- `pinterest-publishing` — publishing (multi-step + reversible)
- `slack-messaging` — messaging with custom states + provider quirks
- `github-workflow` — six-state workflow lifecycle
- `gcalendar-events` — event-with-time (RSVP, recurring)
- `telegram-messaging` — messaging via integer IDs

Each reference app has unit tests plus a real-API E2E script. Copy a reference as a starting template; reference apps are validation fixtures, not production code.

## Validation

```bash
bun --filter=@holaboss/app-builder-sdk run typecheck
bun --filter=@holaboss/app-builder-sdk run test
```
